messages:
nina.p: Hey team — my spouse needed urgent care in Prague this morning (sprained ankle). Clinic says they need proof that my spouse is covered under my plan before they bill insurer. I don’t have their ID card with me. Can People Ops issue a temporary dependent coverage letter I can show them? Also need to know what to file for reimbursement if they charge me.

leo.benefits: Oh no, hope they
re okay. Short answer: yes we can generate a temporary proof-of-coverage letter (PDF) that includes member name, member ID, dependent name, policy number, and claims contact info. It
cts as verification but is not a guarantee of payment. Do you have the dependentull legal name and DOB?

nina.p: Yes — Mateo Ruiz, DOB 2019-05-02. We dont have a marriage certificate with us. Clinic is asking for a relationship proof to attach to their billing system (they said "authorization/relationship doc").

claims_bot: Automated note: For dependent claims and direct billing, acceptable documents typically include dependent listed on the memberard, birth certificate, marriage certificate, or company-dependent enrollment confirmation. If originals are not available, a company-issued temporary coverage letter plus a government ID/passport for the dependent is commonly accepted by European clinics. Reimbursement portal: https://benefits.redwood.com/claims ("International reimbursement").

leo.benefits: If you can show a passport for Mateo and our temporary letter, many hospitals will accept that. I can also include a short sentence in Czech/English saying the dependent is covered. If the clinic still demands formal enrollment proof, we can email them directly from claims@redwood.com to confirm.

paul.hr: Note on retroactive enrollment: we can start an emergency dependent enrollment request from People Ops, but formal plan enrollment typically needs paperwork and HR approval (takes 3-7 business days). For emergency visits we dont need full enrollment to attempt direct billing; the temporary letter + passport is the fast path.

nina.p: They
re asking for a scanned copy of the memberard too. I only have the digital card in my wallet app on my phone — is a screenshot OK?

leo.benefits: Screenshot of your Redwood digital benefits card is fine. I
 include the temporary letter plus screenshot and the dependent passport page. I
 also ask the clinic to email invoices directly to claims@redwood.com so our claims team can attach provider docs to the claim and pursue direct billing.

emma.claims: If clinic charges you up front, submit for reimbursement and include: itemized invoice, proof of payment (card receipt or bank statement), dependent ID, our temporary letter, and a short note explaining emergency. For currency conversion attach an OANDA screenshot or your card exchange entry. Processing: 2 weeks typical for international, mark "urgent" for emergency travel.

nina.p: Thanks — could you draft the Czech/English line and the temporary letter now? I
 appreciate a quick DM; clinic is asking in 15 mins.

leo.benefits: Drafting now. I
 hand them this copy/paste while I send the PDF:
```
Redwood Inference - Benefits Claims
Policy #: RW-PL-2039
Member: Nina P. (Member ID: 0074421)
Dependent: Mateo Ruiz (DOB: 2019-05-02)
Claims intake: claims@redwood.com
Phone (intl): +1-800-555-0199 (limited multilingual support)

This letter confirms the above dependent is listed on the employer's plan. The provider is authorized to contact the insurer for verification of coverage. This is not a guarantee of payment.
Czech: Tento dopis potvrzuje, e ve stejny rodinn je lenem pojistnj. Poskytovatel je zmocnn kontaktovat pojistitele za uelem oven pokryt.
```

nina.p: Got the DM PDF — clinic accepted the screenshot + letter and will email claims. Thank you so much, huge relief.

paul.hr: Follow-up: once youile, DM People Ops with the claim ref and Ian expedite the dependent enrollment if needed. Also keep originals (passport, marriage cert) for post-trip enrollment.
